title: npm run repin can pin a local build of a commit that is gone
foundBy: session agent, after rewriting unpushed history left store entries for commits no branch holds

evidence.verified: scripts/repin-npm.test.mjs passes all 17 of its tests against this same scripts/repin-npm.mjs. Among them, a store holds two builds of a sibling. The repin takes the newer while the sibling's checkout holds it, the older once its main moves back, and the newer again once it is restored. GitHub CI's `ci` passed on 4332859.

resolution: A local build counts only if its commit is on a branch of the sibling's own checkout beside the consumer, where there is one. A newer build left out that way is named. Without such a checkout, as in a campaign member, the store is taken as it stands.
details: `scripts/repin-npm.mjs` takes the newest local build in the store whatever its commit. After a rebase or a squash, the store still holds builds of the commits that were replaced, and they carry the newest times. So `npm run repin` can pin a version whose commit no branch of the sibling's checkout holds any more.
